scope: human review of the scene-anchor MiniMax-H3 action comparison
summary: The scene-anchor v2 comparison is rejected as a featured demo after user review because robot rendering quality is poor and the three commanded motions are not visually distinct enough.
evidence: The user explicitly reported that all three generated robots have poor quality and that their action differences are not obvious.
The v2 robot-identity proxies were only 0.5975-0.6123 against a 0.72 gate.
The v2 workflow had no explicit per-frame action trajectory and semantic_action_adherence_human_reviewed remained false.
lessons: A pairwise pixel-difference gate cannot substitute for human judgment of robot structure or action readability.
Language-only motion prompts are too underconstrained for a precise action-control demo; explicit pose or trajectory conditioning is required.
limitations: The rejected v2 videos remain useful only as negative evidence and must not remain the featured results.
No exact grasp, transfer, insertion, or wrist-rotation event was accepted.
next_actions: Compile language into visibly separated camera-frame arm trajectories, render action-specific control videos from the high-quality robot anchor, and condition a fresh H3 run on those videos.
